name: dram_w1_id_ratio
code:
def dram_w1_id_ratio(p, hw, cfg) -> float:
    """DRAM time over ideal compute time for the identity (M-fastest) width-1 raster: A panels are the fast-dim panels. One consistent operand byte count, see rationale."""
    gx, gy, sk, b = math.ceil(p.M / cfg.tile_m), math.ceil(p.N / cfg.tile_n), max(1, cfg.split_k), p.bytes_per_element
    tx, ty, mb = cfg.tile_m, cfg.tile_n, max(1, cfg.max_blocks_per_sm)
    it = math.ceil(math.ceil(p.K / sk) / cfg.tile_k); kb = it * cfg.tile_k * b; g = gx * gy
    w = g if g * sk <= hw.sm_count * mb else min(g, hw.sm_count)
    u = (min(gx, w) * tx + min(math.ceil(w / gx), gy) * ty) * kb; comp = (p.M * p.K + p.K * p.N) * b
    dist = min(min(mb, math.ceil(g * sk / hw.sm_count)) * (u if gx <= w else (gx * tx + ty) * kb), comp / sk)
    ops = comp + (max(0.0, sk * g / w * u - comp) if dist > hw.l2_bytes else 0.0)
    split = ((2.0 * (sk - 1) if cfg.split_k_mode == "serial" else sk) * p.M * p.N * b) if sk > 1 else 0.0
    t0 = 2.0 * p.M * p.N * p.K / (hw.peak_tflops_f16 * 1e12)
    return (ops + p.M * p.N * b + split + g * sk * it * cfg.threads * cfg.spill_bytes * 2.0) / (hw.bandwidth_gbps * 1e9) / t0
rationale: ONE consistent DRAM byte count for the width-1 raster that the fixed-sign tm_log_inst tie-break realises (identity, M-fastest, used when M <= N); it replaces tm_dram_ratio + refetch/resident_block_scarcity, which counted the per-wave panel re-reads twice (tm_dram_ratio already re-reads the fast-dim panels once per co-resident wave, and the refetch term added them again). Grid order: M fastest, split-K slices outermost (grid z), so each K-slice pass sweeps the gx x gy tile grid with operand panels of tile x K-slice. Panel reuse happens only inside a K-lockstep window: CTAs launched together run their K loops in step and a panel they share is fetched from DRAM once. The window is one CTA per SM (w = min(tiles, sm_count)); co-resident CTAs of one SM run staggered, so extra blocks per SM do NOT widen it. Exception: when the whole grid is co-resident in one round (tiles*sk <= sm_count*max_blocks_per_sm) every CTA is launched at t=0 and the window is the whole grid. A window fetches the panels it spans, u = (min(gx,w)*tx + min(ceil(w/gx),gy)*ty) * K-slice bytes, and there are tiles/w windows per slice. Across windows a panel is re-used only as an L2 capacity hit: the windows re-sweep the same panels cyclically, so under LRU a re-use hits iff its reuse distance fits hw.l2_bytes (step, no partial credit). The reuse distance is one window's bytes when the fast dim fits a window (gx <= w), else one full sweep of the fast dim ((gx*tx + ty) * K-slice bytes); it is multiplied by the number of co-resident cohorts per SM (their traffic interleaves in L2) and capped by one K-slice's operand footprint (M+N)*K/sk*b (a footprint that fits L2 is fetched once). Operand bytes = compulsory (M*K + K*N)*b plus, when the reuse misses, the windowed excess. Then the C write M*N*b, the split-K partials (2(sk-1) planes serial, sk planes parallel, as tm_dram_ratio) and spill traffic, over hw.bandwidth_gbps and t0 = 2MNK/peak (the unit of tm_dram_ratio). No fitted constants; every number is hw.* or cfg.*. Train check (K1): on 4096x11008x4096 the fast 1-block 128x128 st4 config goes from J1e's DRAM leg 0.937 to 0.557, the same as the 2-block 128x128 identity1 config (0.557); on 8192xN the 128x128 width-1 trap keeps ~2x the DRAM time of 128x256/256x128 (0.93-0.97 vs 0.49-0.50).
